notes.27: Question 27 and Question 28 were Vrai and required no correction. Question 29 was usually correctly identified as Faux. For the correction of the statement it was not sufficient to say le public a aimé le premier roman. The answer son roman était un énorme succès was a common correct answer. Question 30 was usually correctly identified as Faux. The correction proved to be quite demanding with elle publie seulement son meilleur travail being a commonly chosen but insufficient answer. Question 31 was usually correctly identified as Faux. The correction was found to be quite challenging and often candidates were tempted to refer to the humour or the style of Amélie’s stories rather than their autobiographical nature. Question 32 was usually correctly identified as Faux. This was the correction where candidates had most success. Exercise 2 Questions 33-40 This final comprehension exercise was, as intended, the most demanding part of the paper and many candidates found it quite challenging. Most could clearly access the general meaning of the text and generally understood the questions, though some candidates were not always sure of the meanings of common question words (quel, comment, qu’est-ce que etc.). Many were able to locate the correct part of the text relevant to the question, but they were often not selective enough in formulating an answer. Some were unable to manipulate their answer sufficiently to give an acceptable response. In this exercise, candidates need to be able to make the necessary changes between direct and reported speech and to deal with the resulting pronoun / possessive adjective confusion. Most candidates were able to score on Question 33, though some answers were invalidated by the candidates’ inappropriate ‘lifting’ of the whole of the first sentence of the text. Question 34 caused few difficulties for candidates. A lot of candidates managed to score at least 1 mark for Question 35(i) and (ii) even when they had found other questions in this exercise difficult. Question 36 was generally well answered. Although, on the face of it, Question 37 seemed straightforward (requiring an answer along the lines of dans/avec un sac à dos), candidates often invalidated their answers with inappropriate additions (e.g. reference to the contents of the rucksack) or by not selecting from the text carefully enough (e.g. d’un sac à dos). A lot of candidates managed to score at least 1 mark on Question 38, even when they had found other questions in this exercise difficult. While Question 39 was generally well answered, Question 40 was found to be the most challenging on this exercise.
notes.40: Question 40 was found to be the most challenging on this exercise. Many candidates were not able to formulate a correct sentence in French to express the key concept. FRENCH (Foreign Language)
notes.key_messages: To maximise their chances of success on this paper, candidates should: • check that they have answered all questions. • read all questions carefully, especially question words (e.g. où, qu’est-ce que, qui). • keep their answers to comprehension questions brief but focused. • check the accuracy of their French, especially in the essay in Section 2. • write relevantly, and no more than the required amount, for the writing tasks.
notes.general_comments: The paper proved accessible to almost all candidates. This paper followed the style and format of previous years and candidates appeared to be familiar with the range of tasks required of them. The vast majority attempted all sections and exercises on the paper and it was evident that they had ample time to complete the paper. With that in mind, candidates should show more evidence of checking of work. Any time left after they have finished may profitably be spent checking that they have answered all the questions, that where they have been able to use material directly from the text it has been copied correctly, and that where they have changed their mind about the answer to a question, their final answer is clear. Standards of legibility and presentation were generally good but candidates should be advised that answers written in pencil then rubbed out and/or overwritten in pen can be difficult to read when scripts are scanned for marking.
